lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p21 - Listen and say.

details: Listen and say introduces the target sound /aɪ/ and its three spellings (ie, y, igh). Students listen to the audio and repeat the sound to practise correct pronunciation.
Look for attentive listening and clear repetition of the 'I' sound, recognising it is the same sound despite different spellings.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p21 - Trace. Then write.

details: Trace and Write develops fine motor skills and letter formation. Students trace the graphemes 'ie', 'y', and 'igh' to build muscle memory and then write them independently.
Look for correct pencil grip and neat formation of the letters, keeping the 'igh' trigraph letters close together.

details: Listen, Point and Say checks understanding of word meaning and sound-symbol correspondence. Listen and point shows they match the spoken word to the right image.
Look for correct pointing to the specific images (cry, night, pie, firefighter, tie, fly) and clear pronunciation of the long 'I' sound.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p67 - Say and then match.

details: Say and match assesses phonemic classification and spelling recognition. Students identify the object and draw a line connecting it to the correct spelling pattern (ie, y, or igh).
Look for logical connections: Tie/Pie to 'ie', Fly/Cry to 'y', Night/Firefighter to 'igh'.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p21 - Underline the /ai/ sound in each word.

details: Underline the sound develops phonemic awareness and orthographic mapping. Students scan the written words and underline the specific letters that make the /aɪ/ sound.
Look for accurate underlining of 'y' in cry/fly, 'igh' in night/firefighter, and 'ie' in pie/tie.

lessonPlan.topic: Numbers Book p100 - 1. Look and write.

details: Look and write connects digits to written words in a vocational context. Students identify the job character and write the corresponding number word (twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty) next to them.
